strings.d1.s0.name: Playa Delfines
strings.d1.s0.tips: Cancún's biggest free beach: no hotels, turquoise Caribbean water. Check for sargassum season (May to August).
strings.d1.s1.name: Cancún Sign Playa Delfines
strings.d1.s1.tips: Colourful CANCUN letters, perfect for photos.
strings.d1.s2.name: El Fish Fritanga
strings.d1.s2.tips: Local fish restaurant on the lagoon. Try the ceviche and tikin xic (grilled marinated fish); rare value for the Hotel Zone.
strings.d1.s3.name: Museo Maya de Cancún
strings.d1.s3.tips: Maya museum with the San Miguelito ruins; an air-conditioned afternoon option.
strings.d1.s4.name: Playa Chac Mool
strings.d1.s4.tips: Central public beach for sunset and waves.
strings.d1.b0.name: Mercado 28 Los De Pescado
strings.d1.b0.tips: Fish tacos in the downtown market, a spot for locals.
strings.d1.b1.name: Playa Tortugas
strings.d1.b1.tips: Calm beach on the lagoon side, next to the ferry dock.
strings.d2.s0.name: Ultramar Feribot Puerto Juárez
strings.d2.s0.tips: 20-minute ferry (about 28 USD return). Rent a golf cart on the island (about 800 MXN).
strings.d2.s1.name: Playa Norte
strings.d2.s1.tips: One of the world's best beaches: shallow and calm, loungers 100-200 MXN.
strings.d2.s2.name: Punta Sur Isla Mujeres
strings.d2.s2.tips: The island's southern tip, with the Ixchel temple ruin and a sculpture park. Mexico's first sunrise.
strings.d2.s3.name: Mango Cafe Isla Mujeres
strings.d2.s3.tips: Caribbean breakfast and lunch; the coconut French toast is the island's famous dish.
strings.d2.s4.name: MUSA Underwater Museum Snorkelling
strings.d2.s4.tips: 500 underwater sculptures. Snorkelling tours leave from the pier; catch the 17:30 ferry back.
strings.d2.b0.name: Isla Mujeres Mercado Municipal
strings.d2.b0.tips: Cheap local food at the municipal market.
strings.d2.b1.name: Garrafón Reef Park
strings.d2.b1.tips: Zipline and snorkelling park, an alternative to MUSA.
strings.d3.s0.name: Chichén Itzá
strings.d3.s0.tips: 2.5 hours from Cancún (ADO bus or tour). See the Kukulkan pyramid and ball court; at the 08:00 opening it is cool and empty. Entry about 697 MXN.
strings.d3.s1.name: Cenote Ik Kil
strings.d3.s1.tips: 5 minutes from Chichén. An open cenote 26 m deep with hanging vines; life jacket compulsory.
strings.d3.s2.name: Valladolid Casa Tía Micha
strings.d3.s2.tips: Yucatán cuisine in Valladolid: cochinita pibil (slow-roasted pork) and sopa de lima (lime soup).
strings.d3.s3.name: Valladolid Calzada de los Frailes
strings.d3.s3.tips: Pastel-coloured colonial street leading to the Convent of San Bernardino.
strings.d3.s4.name: Cenote Suytun
strings.d3.s4.tips: Cave cenote with a famous beam of light; best in afternoon light. The return trip takes 2 hours.
strings.d3.b0.name: Cenote Zací Valladolid
strings.d3.b0.tips: A cenote in the town itself, instead of Suytun.
strings.d3.b1.name: El Mesón del Marqués Valladolid
strings.d3.b1.tips: Colonial restaurant on the main square.
strings.d4.s0.name: Tulum Ruins
strings.d4.s0.tips: 2 hours from Cancún. A Maya fortress by the sea, opening at 08:00; entry about 95 MXN plus a parking fee. Look out for iguanas.
strings.d4.s1.name: Playa Ruinas Tulum
strings.d4.s1.tips: The beach below the ruins, good for a short swim.
strings.d4.s2.name: Gran Cenote
strings.d4.s2.tips: Cave cenote for snorkelling, with turtles and stalactites. The water is clearest in the morning.
strings.d4.s3.name: Taquería Honorio Tulum
strings.d4.s3.tips: Tulum's legendary breakfast and lunch taco spot; cochinita and lechón (suckling pig), sold out by 14:00.
strings.d4.s4.name: Tulum Beach Road
strings.d4.s4.tips: Palm-lined coast road. Choose a beach club (Papaya Playa) or a public beach (Playa Paraíso).
strings.d4.b0.name: Cenote Dos Ojos
strings.d4.b0.tips: A cave system with two "eyes", instead of Gran Cenote.
strings.d4.b1.name: Antojitos La Chiapaneca
strings.d4.b1.tips: Al pastor in Tulum town; an evening stop.
strings.d5.s0.name: Xcaret Park
strings.d5.s0.tips: Underground rivers, a Maya village and an evening show (about 150 USD). 1 hour from Cancún; lunch is included in the Plus package.
strings.d5.s1.name: Xcaret Buffet
strings.d5.s1.tips: Buffet inside the park, included in the Plus package.
strings.d5.s2.name: Xcaret México Espectacular
strings.d5.s2.tips: A show on Mexican history with 300 performers; included in the park ticket.
strings.d5.b0.name: Playa del Carmen Quinta Avenida
strings.d5.b1.name: El Fogón Playa del Carmen
strings.d5.b1.tips: Al pastor tacos in Playa, as an alternative to the park.
strings.d6.s0.name: Chiquilá Ferry Holbox
strings.d6.s0.tips: 2.5 hours from Cancún plus a 20-minute ferry. A car-free island.
strings.d6.s1.name: Holbox Punta Cocos
strings.d6.s1.tips: Shallow, warm lagoon with flamingos and hammock bars.
strings.d6.s2.name: Holbox Roots Pizza
strings.d6.s3.name: Holbox Punta Mosquito Sandbar
strings.d6.s3.tips: A sandbar you can walk to at low tide. Come for sunset, or a whale shark tour from May to September.
strings.d6.b0.name: Holbox Las Panchas
strings.d6.b1.name: Isla Contoy Tour
strings.d6.b1.tips: Bird island with snorkelling off Isla Mujeres, instead of Holbox or Cozumel.
strings.d7.s0.name: Mercado 28
strings.d7.s0.tips: Downtown crafts market: hammocks and silver, with 40% haggling room.
strings.d7.s1.name: Cocina La Chaya Mercado 28
strings.d7.s1.tips: Yucatán home cooking: panuchos (stuffed fried tortillas) and chaya juice. A farewell meal.
strings.d7.s2.name: Parque de las Palapas
strings.d7.s2.tips: Downtown square with marquesitas (crispy crepes) stalls in the evening; quiet by day.
strings.d7.s3.name: ADO Airport Bus
strings.d7.s3.tips: ADO from downtown to the airport takes 30 minutes; time to say goodbye.
strings.d7.b0.name: Taquería Los Charros Cancún
strings.d7.b0.tips: Tacos downtown, instead of the market.
strings.d7.b1.name: Playa Langosta
strings.d7.b1.tips: One last swim in the Hotel Zone.
strings.note0: The Hotel Zone R1/R2 bus costs 15 MXN. ADO buses run to Chichén, Tulum and Playa. A hire car gives you freedom for the cenotes (insurance is expensive).
strings.note1: December to April is dry and 28°C, but it is the busiest and priciest period (Christmas, March spring break). November and April are the sweet spot.
strings.note2: Reach Chichén Itzá and Tulum at the 08:00 opening; by midday it is 35°C and tour buses arrive. Non-biodegradable sunscreen is banned in the cenotes.
strings.note3: Hotel Zone restaurants are 3-5 times pricier; Mercado 28 and downtown (Parque de las Palapas) have local prices. Pay in pesos; the dollar rate is poor.
strings.note4: Tip 10-15%; say 'no gracias' to beach vendors. Drink bottled water.
strings.note5: Ferries: Isla Mujeres from Puerto Juárez (Hotel Zone piers are pricier), Cozumel from Playa, Holbox from Chiquilá.
